node.text: 已解出 45 题 · 作文范文 2 篇

21. Which team will play the most games at the stadium this month? A. Washington Commanders. B. Los Angeles Rams. C. Los Angeles Chargers. D. New Orleans Saints. 答案：B 原文明确说公羊队每赛季在此主场作战次数最多。
22. Which hotel is the nearest to the stadium? A. Sonder Lum Hotel. B. The Ritz-Carlton Los Angeles. C. The H Hotel Los Angeles. D. The Renaissance LA Airport Hotel 答案：A Sonder Lum Hotel就在体育场街对面，距离最近。
23. What do you need to do if you want to park at the stadium? A. Call the parking staff. B. Prepav the parking fee. C. Obtain a parking pass. D. Choose a parking zone. 答案：C 原文建议通过ParkWhiz提前购买停车通行证。
24. What does Kevin usually do to get the meaning of a word? A. Use electronic devices. B. Consult a paper dictionary. C. Guess from the context. D. Turn to his English teacher. 答案：A Kevin认为查词用手机即可，说明他常用电子设备。
25. How did Kevin feel while looking up the word in the dictionary? A. Annoyed. B. Disappointed. C. Encouraged. D. Astonished. 答案：D 他发现整页都是相同开头字母的词，感到震惊又敬畏。
26. What can we learn about the author's first dictionary? A. It helped her through the college. B. It was given to Kevin as a gift. C. It bore witness to her efforts. D. It was a valuable limited edition. 答案：C 作者在词典上逐条做标记，词典见证了她的努力。
27. What has the author come to realize about learning? A. It is never too late to start. B. Motivation is what really matters. C. Children need role models. D. Dictionaries are still a useful tool. 答案：B 作者领悟到关键是想认识单词的好奇心和渴望，即动机。
28. What does the new study imply regarding oaks and sweetgums? A. They affect the growth of other trees. B. They absorb less carbon than expected. C. They harm people's health indirectly. D. They raise the local temperature slowly. 答案：C 橡树释放的异戊二烯与氮氧化物生成臭氧，间接危害健康。
29. Which of the following may Commane suggest based on their study? A. Cutting down the isoprene-producing trees. B. Suspending tree-planting for a few decades. C. Changing the species of trees in new plantings. D. Removing isoprene released by existing trees. 答案：C Commane强调种树要谨慎，暗示应改变树种选择。
30. What does the underlined phrase “oblivious to” in paragraph 5 mean? A. Honest about. B. Unaware of. C. Related to. D. Optimistic about. 答案：B oblivious to意为“未意识到”，即unaware of。
31. What would Auyeung probably advocate? A. Reducing car use in daily life. B. Providing animals with new habitats. C. Controlling population growth. D. Doing more research on the problem. 答案：A Auyeung主张反思以汽车为中心的生活方式，即减少用车。
32. What was the task of the “beauty” group? A. Matching line drawings with objects. B. Rating how beautiful each object was. C. Creating their own clay objects. D. Describing their daily worries. 答案：B “美”组被要求给每件物品的美感打分。
33. According to the study, which group was more likely to think beyond daily life? A. The beauty group, who showed greater interest in bigger questions. B. The beauty group, who felt much happier afterwards. C. The control group, who showed stronger abstract thinking. D. The control group, who felt more enlightened. 答案：A 美组抽象思维得分更高，对人生大问题更感兴趣。
34. Why did the researchers ask about the participants' feelings? A. To compare the two groups' scores. B. To judge their specific thinking pattern. C. To measure the difficulty of the task. D. To identify the true factor behind the results. 答案：D 询问情绪是为排除心情因素，锁定真正原因。
35. What does the study encourage people to do? A. Visit galleries more often. B. Spend less time on screens. C. Buy handmade ceramics. D. Develop their critical thinking. 答案：B 研究建议人们放慢脚步欣赏美，减少对屏幕的依赖。
36. Museums, once silent halls of the past, are now using artificial intelligence (AI) in surprising ways. Walk into many modern galleries today and an AI-powered guide can chat with you, answer your questions, and share fascinating stories about the works on display. 36__________. A. These capabilities make AI a powerful tool for art restoration. B. Visitor data, if misused, could lead to serious privacy issues. C. In short, AI is changing the museum experience in many respects. D. It tailors recommendations to different ages and learning styles. 答案：C 该句总结AI在多方面改变博物馆体验，承上启下。
37. The ways in which AI assists visitors are truly surprising. 37__________ Virtual guides can respond in dozens of languages and adjust their tone to suit each listener, whether a young student or a lifelong art lover. A. These capabilities make AI a powerful tool for art restoration. B. Visitor data, if misused, could lead to serious privacy issues. C. In short, AI is changing the museum experience in many respects. D. It tailors recommendations to different ages and learning styles. 答案：D 后文讲多语言、按听众调整语气，即个性化推荐。
38. AI can also examine artworks in fine detail, far beyond what is possible with human eyes. 38__________ Moreover, it can predict how a fragile painting may age over the years, allowing experts to step in before any visible damage appears. A. These capabilities make AI a powerful tool for art restoration. B. Visitor data, if misused, could lead to serious privacy issues. C. In short, AI is changing the museum experience in many respects. D. It tailors recommendations to different ages and learning styles. E. Museums have always been important places for learning. F. Furthermore, AI chatbots are replacing traditional audio guides. G. AI is also used to design more attractive exhibits. 答案：A 后文讲预测画作老化，说明AI是修复的有力工具。
39. Beyond preservation, AI creates tailored experiences for individual visitors and their families. 39__________ For instance, a curious child and a trained art expert standing before the same painting might each receive a completely different guided tour. A. These capabilities make AI a powerful tool for art restoration. B. Visitor data, if misused, could lead to serious privacy issues. C. In short, AI is changing the museum experience in many respects. D. It tailors recommendations to different ages and learning styles. E. Museums have always been important places for learning. F. Furthermore, AI chatbots are replacing traditional audio guides. G. AI is also used to design more attractive exhibits. 答案：D 后文举例不同观众获得不同导览，说明量身定制。
40. Yet the growing use of AI also raises concerns. These systems depend on collecting vast amounts of personal information through their data-driven algorithms. 40________ Strict rules are therefore needed to ensure that every visitor's privacy is fully protected. A. These capabilities make AI a powerful tool for art restoration. B. Visitor data, if misused, could lead to serious privacy issues. C. In short, AI is changing the museum experience in many respects. D. It tailors recommendations to different ages and learning styles. E. Museums have always been important places for learning. F. Furthermore, AI chatbots are replacing traditional audio guides. G. AI is also used to design more attractive exhibits. 答案：B 前文讲收集大量个人信息，此处应接隐私风险。
41. The 41 ______ that people only really knew Ohio for the three C's - Cleveland, Cincinnati, or Columbus (not Cortland!) - came quickly when I decided to go to school in central Pennsylvania. A. fantasy B. prejudice C. realization D. expectation 答案：C 离开俄亥俄上学后才意识到别人只知三大城市，是“领悟”。
42. Half of my peers didn't even realize I lived a 42 ______ three and a half hours away. A. only B. indeed C. still D. even 答案：A 强调仅三个半小时车程，用only。
43. The 43 ______ are never-ending. A. tests B. questions C. games D. debates 答案：B 前文列举一连串提问，故问题是没完没了的。
44. I was a unicorn in their eyes, a 44 ______ Or, on second thought, maybe just a country hick. A. success B. victim C. novelty D. problem 答案：C 在同学眼中她像独角兽，是新奇罕见的存在。
45. As I grow older, I'm more and more 45 ______ for my small town roots. A. thankful B. hopeful C. suitable D. reliable 答案：A be thankful for表示对小镇根源心怀感激。
46. Sure, my friends and I loved to 46 ______ about how bored we were in the middle of nowhere, 47 ______, as I finish up my junior year of college, I'm convinced that it took 48 ______ our small town to realize how much we actually did love it and what exactly we loved about it. A. dream B. lie C. hear D. complain 答案：D complain about抱怨在偏僻之地无聊。
47. Sure, my friends and I loved to 46 ______ about how bored we were in the middle of nowhere, 47 ______, as I finish up my junior year of college, I'm convinced that it took 48 ______ our small town to realize how much we actually did love it and what exactly we loved about it. A. therefore B. however C. instead D. otherwise 答案：B 前后为转折关系，用however。
48. Sure, my friends and I loved to 46 ______ about how bored we were in the middle of nowhere, 47 ______, as I finish up my junior year of college, I'm convinced that it took 48 ______ our small town to realize how much we actually did love it and what exactly we loved about it. A. touring B. challenging C. leaving D. protecting 答案：C 离开小镇后才意识到自己多爱它。
49. For one, the pace of life isn't anxiety provoking and people really 49______ connecting to each other. A. value B. admit C. fear D. remember 答案：A 人们真正重视彼此间的联系，value符合语境。
50. That means that you do more than just talk to your next door neighbors - in a lot of cases, they're truly an 50______ of your family. A. advantage B. example C. owner D. extension 答案：D 邻居简直是家庭的延伸，an extension of。
51. So much of this 51______ revolves around being outside and knowing the ins and outs of the town, being present and mindful of your 52______ is a critical part of the culture. A. lifestyle B. landscape C. procedure D. personality 答案：A 这种生活方式围绕户外活动展开，lifestyle。
52. So much of this 51______ revolves around being outside and knowing the ins and outs of the town, being present and mindful of your 52______ is a critical part of the culture. A. findings B. surroundings C. belongings D. greetings 答案：B 留意周围环境是文化的重要部分，surroundings。
53. As I move through my college years, I 53 ______ the visits to my little hometown. A. give up B. put off C. face up to D. look forward to 答案：D 大学期间期待回小镇探访，look forward to。
54. I am grateful for the 54 ______ that I had growing up and know that wherever my next adventure takes me, I can 55 ______ my small town roots to lead me in the right direction. 答案：C 感激成长中拥有的童年，childhood。
55. I am grateful for the 54 ______ that I had growing up and know that wherever my next adventure takes me, I can 55 ______ my small town roots to lead me in the right direction. 答案：B 无论去哪，都能依靠小镇根源指引方向，rely on。
56. It is also common for them 56____ (hold) on traditional Chinese holidays such as the Spring Festival, also known as the Chinese New Year, and Mid-Autumn Festival, as well as other local festivals. 答案：to be held it is common for sth to be done，且大集是被举办的，用被动不定式。
57. The exact dates and 57____ (frequent) of dajis vary from region to region. 答案：frequency 与dates并列作主语，需名词形式。
58. Dajis evolved from the folk custom of trading goods, which can be traced back to 58 ____ Han Dynasty (202 B.C.-A.D. 220). 答案：the 朝代前用定冠词the Han Dynasty。
59. In the old days, transportation and communication 59 ____ (be) so poor that it was challenging for households to exchange items to meet their needs for daily 60 ____ (necessity). 答案：were 主语为复数且叙述过去，用were。
60. In the old days, transportation and communication 59 ____ (be) so poor that it was challenging for households to exchange items to meet their needs for daily 60 ____ (necessity). 答案：necessities daily necessities日常必需品，用复数。
61. They would trade their surplus items 61 ____ the goods they needed. 答案：for trade A for B用介词for。
62. Today, residents from surrounding areas flock to these markets. 62____ (Draw) by the enticing aromas, they hurry to food stalls, 63____ steamed dumplings and hot noodle soups. 答案：Drawn 过去分词作状语，表被香气吸引。
63. Today, residents from surrounding areas flock to these markets. 62____ (Draw) by the enticing aromas, they hurry to food stalls, 63____ steamed dumplings and hot noodle soups. 答案：for hurry to...for...表示赶去摊位买某物。
64. Before 64 ____ (head) back home, they purchase some fresh fruit and vegetables from local farmers, which are much 65 ____ (cheap)than those in supermarkets, and embark on their journey back home. 答案：heading before后接动名词heading。
65. Before 64 ____ (head) back home, they purchase some fresh fruit and vegetables from local farmers, which are much 65 ____ (cheap)than those in supermarkets, and embark on their journey back home. 答案：cheaper much修饰比较级，用cheaper。
